translations.text: In the eighth month, in the second year of King Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah the prophet, son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, and he said:
The Lord was angry with your fathers with great anger, and he said to them:
Thus says the Lord Almighty: Return to me, says the Lord of hosts, and I will return to you, says the Lord of hosts;

and do not be like your fathers, whom the former prophets rebuked, saying: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Turn now from your evil ways and from your deeds that are not good. But they did not listen to me and did not pay heed to listen to me, says the Lord.
Where are your fathers and the prophets? Will they live forever?

But receive my words and my law, all that I commanded my servants the prophets, which overtook your fathers. And they answered and said: As the Lord Almighty purposed to do to us according to our ways and according to our doings, so he has done to us.

On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, that is, the month of Shebat, in the second year of King Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah the prophet, son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, and he said:
I saw in a vision of the night, and behold, a man mounted on a red horse; and he was standing between the two shady mountains, and behind him were red-dappled horses and white ones.
And I said: What are these, Lord? And the angel who was speaking with me said to me: I will show you what these are.
And the man who was standing between the two mountains answered me and said to me: These are the ones whom the Lord has sent out to go to and fro over the earth.
And they answered the angel of the Lord who was standing between the two mountains, and said: We have gone throughout the whole earth, and behold, the whole earth is inhabited and at rest.
And the angel of the Lord answered and said: O Lord Almighty, how long will you not have mercy on Jerusalem and on the cities of Judah, which you have disregarded? This is now seventy years.
And the Lord Almighty answered the angel who was speaking with me with good words and words of comfort.
And the angel who was speaking with me said to me: Cry out and say: Thus says the Lord Almighty: I have been jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with a great jealousy,
and with great anger I am angry with the nations that rose up against them, because I was angry only a little, but they joined together against them for evil.
Therefore thus says the Lord: I will return to Jerusalem with mercy; my house will be built in it, says the Lord Almighty, and once again a measuring line will be stretched out over Jerusalem.

And the angel who was speaking with me said to me: Cry out and say: Thus says the Lord Almighty: The cities will once again spread out in prosperity, and the Lord will again have mercy on Zion, and Jerusalem will again be pleasing to him.
And I lifted up my eyes and saw four horns.
And I said to the angel who was speaking with me: What are these, Lord? And he said to me: These are the horns that scattered Judah and Jerusalem and Israel.
And the Lord showed me four craftsmen.

And I said to him, "What are these coming to do?" And he said, "These are the horns that crushed them, and none of them lifted up his head. And these have come out to sharpen them for their hands. These four horns are the nations that lifted up their horns against the land of the Lord to scatter it."
And I lifted up my eyes and looked, and behold, a man, and in his hand he had a line for measuring land.
And I said to him, "Where are you going?" And he said to me, "To measure Jerusalem, and to see how great its breadth is and how great its length is."
And the angel who was speaking with me was standing there, and another angel was coming out to meet him.
And he answered him and said, "Run and say to that young man: Jerusalem shall be inhabited abundantly, because of the multitude of people and cattle within it.
And I will be to it a wall of fire round about, and I will be the glory in its midst."
"O, O, flee from the land of the north," says the Lord, "for I will gather you from the four winds of heaven," says the Lord.
"Escape to Zion, you who dwell with the daughter of Babylon."
For thus says the Lord Almighty: "After glory he has sent me to the nations that plundered you, for whoever touches you is like one who touches the pupil of his eye.
For behold, I will bring my hand upon them, and they shall become spoil for those who served them, and you shall know that the Lord Almighty has sent me."
"Rejoice and be glad, O Zion, for behold, I am coming, and I will dwell in your midst," says the Lord.
"And many nations shall flee for refuge to the Lord on that day, and they shall become his people, and they shall dwell in your midst, and you shall know that the Lord Almighty has sent me to you.
And the Lord shall take possession of Judah as his portion in the holy land, and Jerusalem shall again be pleasing to him.
Let all flesh fear before the face of the Lord, for he has risen up out of his holy clouds."
And the Lord showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the Lord, and the devil was standing at his right hand to oppose him.
And the Lord said to the devil, "May the Lord rebuke you, devil; may the Lord who chose Jerusalem rebuke you. Is not this man, behold, like a burning brand snatched out of the fire?"
And Joshua was clothed in filthy garments, and he stood before the face of the angel.

And he answered and said to those standing before him, "Take those filthy garments off him." And he said to him, "Behold, I have taken your iniquities away from you." And he said, "Clothe him in a full-length robe."
"And put a holy turban on his head." And they clothed him in garments.
And the angel of the Lord bore witness to Joshua and said:
"Thus says the Lord Almighty: If you walk in my ways and keep my commandments, you shall judge my house; and if you guard my courts, I will grant you to walk among these who stand here.
Hear now, O Joshua the high priest, you and your companions who sit before you, for they are men who watch for signs. For behold, I will bring my servant; the Dawn is his name."

For the stone which I have set before the face of Joshua: on that one stone are seven eyes. Behold, I will dig a pit, says the Lord Almighty, and I will lay my hand on all the falsehood of that land in one day.
Says the Lord Almighty: each man shall call his neighbour under his vine and under his fig tree.
And the angel who spoke with me came back and woke me, as a man is woken from his sleep,
and he said to me: What do you see? And I said: Behold, I have seen a lampstand of gold, solid throughout, and a lamp on it, and seven mouths to the lamp, which are on its top.
And there were two olive trees by it, one on the right of its lamp and one on the left.
And I asked the angel who spoke with me, and I said: What are these, lord?
And the angel who spoke with me answered and said to me: Do you not know what these are? And I said: No, lord.
And he answered and said to me: This is the word of the Lord to Zerubbabel, saying: Not by great might, nor by power, but by my Spirit, says the Lord Almighty.
Who are you, O great mountain, before Zerubbabel, to make the way straight? And I will bring out the stone of the inheritance; its grace shall be equal to grace.
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house, and his hands shall complete it; and you shall know that the Lord Almighty has sent me to you.

For who has despised the day of small things? They shall rejoice, and shall see the stone of captivity [?] in the hand of Zerubbabel. The seven are the eyes of the Lord, which look over all the earth.
And I answered and said to him: What are these two olive trees, on the right of the lampstand and on its left?

And I asked again a second time and said to him: What are these two branches of the olive trees, which are in the hands of these golden spouts [?], which pour in and draw up into the golden mouths of the lamp?
And he spoke and said to me: Do you not know what these are? And I said: No, lord.
And he said: These two are the sons of fatness, who stand before the Lord of all the earth.
And I turned, and lifted up my eyes, and looked; and behold, a flying sickle.
And he said to me: What do you see? And I said: I see a flying sickle, twenty cubits long and ten cubits wide.

And he said to me: This is the curse that goes out over the face of all the earth; for every thief shall be punished by it, even to death, and every false swearer shall likewise be punished by it, even to death.

And I will send it out, says the Lord Almighty, and it shall enter the house of the thief, and the house of the one who swears falsely by my name; and it shall lodge in the midst of his house, and shall consume its timber and its stones.
And the angel who spoke with me went out and said to me: Lift up your eyes and see what is going out.
And I said: What is this measure, lord, that is going out? And he said: This is their falsehood in all the earth. And I looked,
and behold, a talent of lead was lifted up; and then, behold, a woman was sitting in the middle of the measure.
And he said: This is lawlessness. And he threw her down into the middle of the measure, and threw the lump of lead onto its mouth.

And I lifted up my eyes and saw two women coming out, and they were made winged, and there was wind in their wings, and their wings were like the wings of a hoopoe. And they lifted up the measure between heaven and earth.
And I said to the angel who was speaking with me: Where are they carrying this measure?
And he said to me: To build houses for it in the land of Babylon, and to prepare it; and they will set it there in its prepared place.
And I turned and lifted up my eyes and looked, and behold, four chariots were coming out from between two mountains, and the mountains were mountains of bronze.
In the first chariot were red [?] horses, and in the second chariot black horses,
and in the third chariot white horses, and in the fourth chariot dappled-grey [?] horses.
And I answered and said to the angel who was speaking with me: What are these, lord?
And the angel answered and said to me: These are the four winds of heaven, which go out to stand before the Lord of all the earth.
The chariot with the black horses went out to the land of the north, and the white ones went out after them, and the dappled ones went out to the land of the south.
And the red [?] ones went out and were looking about to go to and fro through the earth. And he said: Go throughout the earth. And they went throughout the earth.
And he cried out and spoke to me, saying: Behold, those who are going to the land of the north have set my anger at rest in the region of the north.
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Take from the captives: from the rulers, from its useful men, and from those who have known it. And on that day go into the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah, who has come from Babylon.
And he took silver and gold, and make crowns, and set them on the head of Joshua son of Jozadak, the high priest.
And say to him: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Behold, a man whose name is the Rising, and from beneath him it shall spring up, and he shall build the house of the Lord.
And he himself shall receive virtue, and shall sit and rule upon his throne, and the priest shall be at his right hand, and there shall be a counsel of peace between the two of them.
But the crown shall belong to those who endure, and to its useful men, and to those who have known it, and it shall be for the favour of the son of Zephaniah and for a hymn in the house of the Lord.

And those who are far off from them shall come and build the house of the Lord, and you shall know that the Lord Almighty has sent me to you. And it shall be so if you truly listen to the voice of the Lord your God.
And in the fourth year of King Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah on the fourth day of the ninth month, which is Chislev.
And Arasar and Arbosargir the king, and his men, sent to Bethel to make propitiation for them before the Lord,
and they spoke to the priests in the house of God Almighty and to the prophets, saying: Has the holy offering come in here in the fifth month, as they used to do then, for many years?
And the word of the Lord of hosts came to me, saying:
Say to all the people of the land and to the priests: If you fasted or mourned in the fifth or the seventh month, behold, for these seventy years, was it really for me that you fasted?
And if you ate or drank, was it not you yourselves who ate and you yourselves who drank?

Are these not the words that the Lord spoke by the hand of his prophets who came before, when Jerusalem was inhabited and prosperous, and her cities around her, and the hill country and the lowland were inhabited?
And the word of the Lord came to Zechariah, saying:
Thus says the Lord Almighty: Judge with true judgment, and each of you show mercy and compassion to his brother.
Do not oppress the widow, the orphan, the stranger, or the poor, and let none of you plot evil in his heart against his brother.
But they refused to pay attention. They turned their backs in contempt and made their ears heavy so that they would not hear.

They made their hearts stubborn so that they would not hear my law and my words, which the Lord Almighty sent by his Spirit, by the hand of the former prophets. And there was great wrath from the Lord Almighty.
And it shall be that, just as he spoke and they did not listen to him, so they too will cry out to me and I will not listen to them, says the Lord Almighty.

And I scattered them among all the nations whom they did not know. After them this land was laid waste by those who passed through it and those who went back and forth in it, and they made the chosen land a ruin.
And the word of the Lord Almighty came to me, saying:
Thus says the Lord Almighty: I have been jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with great jealousy, and with great anger I have been jealous for her.
Thus says the Lord: I will return to Zion and dwell in the midst of Jerusalem. Jerusalem shall be called the City of Truth, and the mountain of the Lord Almighty the Holy Mountain.
Thus says the Lord Almighty: Old men and old women shall again sit in the streets of Jerusalem, each with his staff in his hand because of his great age.
And the streets of the city shall be filled with boys and girls singing in its streets.
Thus says the Lord Almighty: If it is impossible in the eyes of the remnant of this people in those days, will it also be impossible in my eyes? says the Lord Almighty.
Thus says the Lord Almighty: Behold, I will save my people from the land of the sunrise and from the land of the sunset.
I will bring them in and settle them in the midst of Jerusalem. They shall be my people, and I will be their God in truth and in righteousness.

Thus says the Lord Almighty: Let your hands be strong, you who hear in these days these words from the mouth of the prophets, from the day the foundation of this house of the Lord Almighty was laid, and since the temple has been built.

For before those days people's wages brought no profit, and there was no hire for animals. For those who went out and came in there was no peace from trouble, and I set every man against his neighbor.
But now I will not deal with the remnant of my people as in the former days, says the Lord Almighty.

Instead I will show peace: the vine shall give its fruit, the earth shall yield its seed, and the heavens shall give their dew, and I will give all these things as an inheritance to the remnant of my people.

And it shall be that, just as you were under a curse among the nations, house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will save you, and you shall be in blessing. Do not be afraid, and let your hands be strong.
For thus says the Lord Almighty: Just as I resolved to do you harm because my anger was roused by your fathers, says the Lord Almighty, and I did not relent,
so now I am ready, and in these days I resolve to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. Do not be afraid.
These are the things that you shall do: speak the truth, each of you to his neighbour, and give judgments that make for peace in your gates;
and let none of you plot evil in your hearts against his neighbour, and do not love a false oath, for I hate all these things, says the Lord.
And the word of the Lord Almighty came to me, saying:

Thus says the Lord Almighty: The fast of the fourth month, the fast of the fifth, the fast of the seventh and the fast of the tenth shall become joy and gladness and good feasts for the house of Judah. And you shall rejoice; so love peace and truth.
Thus says the Lord Almighty: Many peoples shall yet come, and they shall dwell in many cities;
and they shall gather together into one city and say, "Let us go and entreat the face of the Lord, and seek the face of the Lord Almighty"; and another shall say, "I will come too."
And many other nations shall come to Jerusalem to seek the face of the Lord Almighty and to ask for favour from the face of the Lord.

Thus says the Lord Almighty: In those days, ten men from all the languages of the nations shall take hold, and they shall grasp the hem of a Jewish man's garment and say to him, "Let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you."
The oracle of the word of the Lord against the land of Hadrach, and Damascus is its sacrifice, for the Lord watches over people and over all the tribes of Israel,
and over Hamath and its territory, and over Tyre and Sidon, for they thought themselves very wise.
And Tyre built its walls, and heaped up silver like dust and gold like the mud of the roads.
Therefore the Lord will take possession of them and strike down her power in the sea, and she herself will be consumed by fire.
Ashkelon will see it and be afraid, and Gaza will be in great anguish, and Ekron too, because she has been put to shame by her sin. The king will perish from Gaza, and Ashkelon will not be inhabited.
And foreigners will settle in Ashdod, and I will cast down the pride of the foreigners;

and I will take their blood out of their mouths and their abominations from between their teeth. These too will be left as a remnant for our God, and they will be like commanders of thousands in Judah, and Ekron like the Jebusite.
And I will set a guard over my house, so that no one goes out or comes back. No oppressor will come against them ever again, for now I have seen it with my own eyes.

Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion; proclaim it, daughter of Jerusalem! Look, your king is coming to you, righteous and a saviour, and he will deliver you. He is gentle, and he rides on a beast of burden and a young colt.

And he shall destroy the chariots from Ephraim and the horses from Jerusalem, and the bow of war shall be destroyed, and abundance and peace from the nations. And he shall rule over the waters as far as the sea, and from the river to the ends of the earth.
And you, by the blood of the covenant, have released your prisoners from the pit that had no water.
Let the prisoners of the congregation sit in the prison, and in place of one day of your sojourning I will repay you double.
For I have bent you, Judah, as a bow for myself, and I [filled?] Ephraim, and I will raise up your sons, O Zion, against the sons of the Greeks, and I will wield you like a sword of war.
And the Lord shall be over them, and he shall go forth like the lightning of an arrow. And the Lord Almighty shall blow the trumpet and shall advance in the tumult of his word.
And the Lord Almighty shall help them, and they shall consume them and bury them with sling-stones. And they shall drink their blood like wine, and they shall fill bowls like the altar.
And on that day the Lord God shall save them as sheep, his own people, for holy stones roll upon his land.
For what is his goodness, and what is his excellence? Food for young men, and fragrant wine for virgins.
Ask the Lord for rain in its season, early and late. The Lord has made wonders, and he will give them winter rain, to each one green plants in the field.
For those who gave oracles spoke trouble, and the diviners spoke false visions, and they told false revelations and gave empty comfort. Therefore they have withered away, for there was no healing.

My anger has been kindled against the shepherds, and I will punish the lambs. And the Lord God Almighty will visit his flock, the house of Judah, and will set them in order like his splendid horses in battle.
From him he looked out, and from him he set things in order, and from him came the bow of wrath. From him shall come forth every [exposer?] against him as well.
And they shall be like warriors who trample the mud in the road in battle, and they shall be drawn up for battle, for the Lord is with them, and those mounted on horses shall be put to shame.

And I will strengthen the house of Judah, and I will save the house of Joseph, and I will settle them, for I have loved them. And they shall be as though I had not turned away from them, for I am the Lord their God, and I will hear them.
And they shall be like the warriors of Ephraim, and their hearts shall rejoice as with wine. And their children shall see it and rejoice, and their hearts shall rejoice in the Lord.
I will make it known to them and I will receive them, for I will save them, and they shall multiply as they were many before.
And I will scatter them among the peoples, and those far off shall remember me. Their children shall grow up, and they shall return.
And I will bring them back from the land of Egypt, and I will receive them from Assyria, and I will bring them into Gilead and Lebanon, and not a single one of them shall be left behind.

And they shall pass through the narrow sea, and they shall strike the waves upon the sea, and all the depths of the rivers shall dry up. And the insolence of the Assyrians shall be taken from them, and the scepter of Egypt shall be removed from them.
And I will strengthen them in the Lord their God, and they shall boast in his name. Thus says the Lord.
Open your gates, O Lebanon, and let fire devour your firs.
Wail, you pines, for the firs have fallen, for the great ones have been made utterly wretched; and wail, you oaks of Bashan, for the forest, the dense plantation, has fallen.
The sound of the shepherds' lament, for their glory has been brought low; the sound of the lions' roaring, for the gathering of the Jordan has been brought low.
Thus says the Lord Almighty: Shepherd the sheep destined for slaughter,
whose owners slaughtered them and did not repent. And those who sold them said, "Blessed be the Lord, for we have become rich"; and their shepherds felt no grief for them.

Therefore I will no longer spare the inhabitants of the land, says the Lord. Behold, I will hand over every man into the hands of his neighbor and into the hands of his king, and they will destroy the land, and I will not rescue them from their hands.
And I will shepherd the sheep destined for slaughter in the land of the Canaanites. And I took for myself two staffs: one I called Goodness, and the other I called Portion; and I shepherded my sheep.
And I removed three shepherds in one month, and my soul grew weary of them, for their soul also howled against me.
And I said: I will not shepherd you. Let what is dying die, and let what is failing fail, and let those who are left eat, each one, the flesh of his neighbor.
And I took my staff, Goodness, and cast it away, to annul my covenant which I had made with all the people.
And it was annulled on that day; and the sheep of the Canaanites, which are kept for me, knew that it is the word of the Lord.
And I said to them: If it seems good to you, give us our wages, or else refuse. And they weighed out my wages to me: thirty pieces of silver.

And the Lord said to me: Put it into the furnace, and see whether it is tested and genuine, in the way that I was tested for them. And I took the thirty pieces of silver and put them in the house of the Lord, into the smelting furnace.
And I cast away the second staff, Portion, to annul the covenant between Judah and Israel.
And the Lord said to me: Take again for yourself the gear of a shepherd, an unskilled shepherd;

for behold, I will raise up a shepherd over the land. He will not look after the failing and the weak, he will not seek out the scattered, he will not heal the broken, he will not care for the healthy; he will eat the flesh of the choice ones and twist their ankles.
O you who shepherd vanity and have abandoned the sheep! A sword upon his arm and upon his right eye: his arm shall wither away completely, and his right eye shall be completely blinded.
An oracle of the word of the Lord concerning Israel. Thus says the Lord, who stretched out the heavens, founded the earth, and forms the spirit of man within him:
Behold, I will make Jerusalem like a shaken doorway to all the peoples around it, and in Judea, and Jerusalem shall be besieged.
And on that day I will make Jerusalem a stone trampled by all the nations; everyone who tramples it will mock it with mockery, and all the races of the earth will gather against it.

On that day, says the Lord Almighty, I will strike every horse with bewilderment and its rider with frenzy; but upon the house of Judah I will open my eyes, and I will strike all the horses of the peoples with blindness.
And the commanders of thousands of Judah will say in their hearts, "We have found for ourselves the inhabitants of Jerusalem through the Lord Almighty, their God."

On that day I will make the commanders of thousands of Judah like firebrands among wood, and like a torch of fire among reeds, and they will devour all the peoples round about, on the right and on the left. And Jerusalem will be inhabited again in its own place, in Jerusalem.
And the Lord will save the dwelling of Judah as at the beginning, so that the boasting of the house of David and the proud exaltation of the inhabitants of Jerusalem may not grow great over Judah.

And on that day the Lord will give help to the inhabitants of Jerusalem. On that day the weak one among them will be like David, and the house of David will be like the house of God, like an angel of the Lord before them.
And on that day I will seek to wipe out all the nations that come against Jerusalem.

And I will pour out on the house of David and on the inhabitants of Jerusalem a spirit of grace and of mercy. They will look upon me, because they mocked me with songs, and they will beat themselves in mourning as for a beloved one, and they will grieve with grief as for a firstborn.
On that day the mourning in Jerusalem will be great, like the mourning for the pomegranate grove (Rhoon) in the plain of the one cut down.
And the land will mourn, tribe by tribe: the tribe of the house of David by itself, and their wives by themselves; the tribe of the house of Nathan by itself;
and the tribe of the house of Levi by itself, and their wives by themselves; the tribe of the house of Simeon by itself, and their wives by themselves;
and all the remaining tribes, each by itself.
On that day every place will be opened to the house of David and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem for removal and for sprinkling.

And on that day, says the Lord of hosts, I will destroy the names of the idols from the land, and there will no longer be any remembrance of them. And I will wipe the false prophets and the unclean spirit from the land.

And if anyone still prophesies, his father and his mother, who bore him, will say to him, "You shall not live, because you have spoken falsehood in the name of the Lord." And his father and his mother, who bore him, will bind him while he is prophesying.
And on that day the prophets will be ashamed, each one of his vision in their prophesying, and for this reason they will put on a goatskin, because they lied.
And he will say, "I am not a prophet, for I am a man who works the land; for a man fathered me from my youth."
And they will say to him, "What are these wounds between your hands?" And he will say, "Those I received when I was wounded in the house of my beloved."

Now, O sword, rise up against the shepherds and against the man who is his fellow citizen, says the Lord Almighty. I will strike the shepherd, and let the sheep be scattered, and I will turn my hand against the shepherds.
And on that day, says the Lord, two parts in it will be destroyed and will perish, and the third part will remain in it.

And I will bring the third part out of the fire, and I will refine it as silver is refined, and I will test them as gold is tested. They will call on my name, and I will hear them and say, "This is my people." And they will say, "You are the Lord my God."
Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when the spoil taken from you will be divided in your midst.

And I will gather all the nations against Jerusalem for battle, and they will take the city, and the houses will be plundered and the women defiled. Half of the city will go out into captivity, but the remnant of my people will not be destroyed from the city.
And the Lord will go out and will be drawn up for battle, as in the days of his battle against the nations, on the day of war.

On that day his feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, which is before Jerusalem on the east. And the Mount of Olives will be split, half of it toward the east and toward the sea, and there will be a very great chasm.

And half of the mountain will [?] toward the north, and half of it toward the south. And the valley of my mountains will be blocked, and the ravine of the mountains will be joined as far as Asael. It will be blocked as it was blocked because of the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah. And the Lord my God will come, and all the holy ones with him.
And on that day it will be like this: there will be no light, and there will be cold and frost
on that one day. That day is known to the Lord. It will be neither day nor night, and at evening there will be light.
And on that day living water will go out from Jerusalem, half of it to the first sea and half of it to the last sea. It will be like this in summer and in winter.
And the Lord will be king over all the earth. On that day the Lord alone will be one, and his name one,

all around the whole land, and the wilderness from Geba to Rimmon, on the back side of Jerusalem. And Ramah will remain in its place, from the Gate of Benjamin to the place of the First Gate, to the Corner Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel to the king's winepresses.
They will dwell in it, and there will be no more curse, and Jerusalem will dwell in hope.

And this will be the plague with which the Lord struck all the peoples who were drawn up against Jerusalem: their flesh will melt away while they stand on their feet, their eyes will flow out of their sockets, and their tongues will melt away in their mouths.
And on that day there will be a great panic from the Lord upon them. Each man will seize the hand of his neighbour, and his hand will be wrapped around his neighbour's neck.
And Judah will be drawn up at Jerusalem and will gather the wealth of all the peoples round about: gold and silver and clothing in very great abundance.
And this will be the plague on the horses, the mules, the camels, the donkeys, and all the livestock that were in that camp, the same as this plague.
And all who are left of those nations that came against Jerusalem will go up year after year to worship the King, the Lord Almighty, and to keep the feast of Tabernacles.
And if any of all the tribes of the earth do not come up to Jerusalem to worship the King, the Lord Almighty, these too will be added to them.
If the tribe of Egypt does not come up and does not come, then on these too will come the plague with which the Lord destroyed all the nations that do not come up to keep the feast of Tabernacles.
This will be the sin of Egypt, and the sin of all the nations that do not come up to keep the feast of Tabernacles.
And on that day, whatever is on the cheek-pieces of the horses shall be holy to the Lord Almighty, and the cauldrons in the house of the Lord shall be like the bowls before the face of the altar.

And every cauldron in Jerusalem and in Judah shall be holy to the Lord Almighty, and all who offer sacrifice shall come and take some of them and set [their offerings] in them [?]. And there shall no longer be a Canaanite in the house of the Lord Almighty on that day, says the Lord Almighty.
